sanskrit: vayam u tvām apūrvya sthūraṁ na kac cid bharanto 'vasyavaḥ | vāje citraṁ havāmahe ||
english: We who seek thy aid, bearing no gift like others to an unrivalled [lord], invoke thee, O brilliant one, for the prize.

sanskrit: upa tvā karmann ūtaye sa no yuvo graś cacrāma yo dhṛṣat | tvām id dhy avitāraṁ vavṛmahe sakhāya indra sānasim ||
english: For thy aid in our work, the bold one who urged us on has approached thee, O young [lord]; for we friends have truly chosen thee, O Indra, as our constant protector.

sanskrit: ā yāhīma indavo 'śvapate gopata urvarāpate | somaṁ somapate piba ||
english: Come hither, lord of horses, lord of cattle, lord of fields; these soma-drops [call thee]: drink the soma, O lord of soma.

sanskrit: vayaṁ hi tvā bandhumantam abandhavo viprāsa indra yemima | yā te dhāmāni vṛṣabha tebhir ā gahi viśvebhiḥ somapītaye ||
english: We inspired poets, though without kinsmen of our own, have held fast thee, O Indra, who art rich in allies; come, O bull, with all thy abodes for the drinking of soma.

sanskrit: sīdantas te vayo yathā gośrīte madhau madire vivakṣaṇe | abhi tvām indra nonumaḥ ||
english: Settling as birds [settle] in the sweet, intoxicating, exhilarating [draught] mixed with milk, we praise thee eagerly, O Indra.

sanskrit: acchā ca tvainā namasā vadāmasi kim muhuś cid vi dīdhayaḥ | santi kāmāso harivo dadiṣ ṭvaṁ smo vayaṁ santi no dhiyaḥ ||
english: We speak to thee with homage and approach thee; why dost thou repeatedly shine elsewhere? Our desires are present, O bay-horsed Indra, we are here, thou art the giver; our prayers too are present.

sanskrit: nūtnā id indra te vayam ūtī abhūma nahi nū te adrivaḥ | vidmā purā parīṇasaḥ ||
english: We have now become new recipients of thy protection, O Indra; truly we lack nothing from thee, O stone-wielder; we have known [thy bounty] of old, in former times abundantly.

sanskrit: vidmā sakhitvam uta śūra bhojyam ā te tā vajrinn īmahe | uto samasminn ā śiśīhi no vaso vāje suśipra gomate ||
english: We know thy friendship and thy gifts of enjoyment, O hero; we seek those [gifts] from thee, O wielder of the vajra; and do thou whet us toward the same [battle], O lord of wealth, in the contest with cattle, O fair-lipped one.

sanskrit: yo na idam-idam purā pra vasya āninaya tam u vaḥ stuṣe | sakhāya indram ūtaye ||
english: Him who formerly led us repeatedly to ever greater good, him I praise for you, O friends — Indra — for our protection.

sanskrit: haryaśvaṁ satpatiṁ carṣaṇīsahaṁ sa hi ṣmā yo amandatan | ā tu naḥ sa vayati gavyam aśvyaṁ stotṛbhyo maghavā śatam ||
english: Him of the bay horses, the true lord, who overpowers the peoples — for he is the one who rejoiced — the bountiful one bestows upon his praisers a hundredfold of cattle and horses.

sanskrit: tvayā ha svid yujā vayam prati śvasantaṁ vṛṣabha bruvīmahi | saṁsthe janasya gomataḥ ||
english: With thee as our ally, O bull, we would indeed challenge the one who threatens [us], in the gathering of the people rich in cattle.

sanskrit: jayema kāre puruhūta kāriṇo 'bhi tiṣṭhema dūḍhyaḥ | nṛbhir vṛtraṁ hanyāma śūśuyāma cāver indra pra ṇo dhiyaḥ ||
english: May we conquer in the contest, O much-invoked Indra, and overcome the deceivers; may we slay Vṛtra with our men, may we prosper; speed forth our thoughts, O Indra.

sanskrit: abhrātṛvyo anā tvam anāpir indra januṣā sanād asi | yudhed āpitvam icchase ||
english: Without a brother's enmity, without a kinsman's [rivalry], O Indra, thou art from birth and from of old without an equal companion; yet thou seekest fellowship even in battle.

sanskrit: nakī revantaṁ sakhyāya vindase pīyanti te surāśvaḥ | yadā kṛṇoṣi nadanuṁ sam ūhasy ād it piteva hūyase ||
english: Thou dost not find a wealthy man for friendship; those of swift horses mock thee; but when thou makest a roar and stirrest everything together, then thou art called upon as a father.

sanskrit: mā te amājuro yathā mūrāsa indra sakhye tvāvataḥ | ni ṣadāma sacā sute ||
english: May we not, like fools grown old at home, O Indra, be parted from the friendship of thee who art such; may we sit together when the soma is pressed.

sanskrit: mā te godatra nir arāma rādhasa indra mā te gṛhāmahi | dṛḻhā cid aryaḥ pra mṛśābhy ā bhara na te dāmāna ādabhe ||
english: May we not fall away from thy bounty, O giver of cattle, O Indra; may we not be deprived of thee; reach forward and bring [gifts] even from the firm [strongholds] of the stranger — thy gifts are not to be deceived.

sanskrit: indro vā ghed iyan maghaṁ sarasvatī vā subhagā dadir vasu | tvaṁ vā citra dāśuṣe ||
english: Either Indra indeed gives this bounty, or the blessed Sarasvatī gives wealth; or thou, O brilliant one, [givest] to the worshipper.

sanskrit: citra id rājā rājakā id anyake yake sarasvatīm anu | parjanya iva tatanad dhi vṛṣṭyā sahasram ayutā dadat ||
english: The brilliant one alone is the true king; the others along the Sarasvatī are but petty kings; like Parjanya he has spread with his rain, giving thousands and ten-thousands.

sanskrit: o tyam ahva ā ratham adyā daṁsiṣṭham ūtaye | yam aśvinā suhavā rudravartanī ā sūryāyai tasthathuḥ ||
english: I have called hither today that most wondrous chariot for our aid — the one which you two Aśvins, easily invoked and driving on a dread path, have set in place for Sūryā.

sanskrit: pūrvāyuṣaṁ suhavam purusp ṛham bhu jyuṁ vājeṣu pūrvyam | sacanāvantaṁ sumatibhiḥ sobhare vidveṣasam anéhasam ||
english: I call that chariot which goes before in life, easily invoked and much desired, foremost in prizes, which brought Bhujyu [to safety]; of good thoughts, without hatred toward Sobhari, and without reproach.

sanskrit: iha tyā purubhūtamā devā namobhir aśvinā | arvācīnā sv avase karāmahe gantārā dāśuṣo gṛham ||
english: Here, the two gods most often praised, the Aśvins, we draw hither with our homage fully toward us for aid — [you] who go to the house of the worshipper.

sanskrit: yuvo rathasya pari cakram īyata īrmānyad vām iṣaṇyati | asmām̐ acchā sumatir vāṁ śubhas patī ā dhenur iva dhāvatu ||
english: The rim of your chariot-wheel revolves [around]; the thong that urges you on stirs itself; may your benevolence, O lords of beauty, come to us as a cow [runs] to her calf.

sanskrit: ratho yo vāṁ trivandhu ro hiraṇyābhīśur aśvinā | pari dyāvāpṛthivī bhūṣati śrutas tena nāsatyā gatam ||
english: The chariot which is yours, O Aśvins, of three joints and golden reins, the renowned one that adorns both heaven and earth — with that, O Nāsatyās, come hither.

sanskrit: daśasyantā manave pūrvyaṁ divi yavaṁ vṛkeṇa karṣathaḥ | tā vām adya sumatibhiḥ śubhas patī aśvinā pra stuvīmahi ||
english: Ministering [with gifts] to Manu, you two plough in heaven the ancient barley with a wolf [as your ploughshare]; the two of you, O lords of beauty, O Aśvins, we now praise with our prayers.

sanskrit: upa no vājinīvasū yātam ṛtasya pathibhiḥ | yebhis tṛkṣiṁ vṛṣaṇā trāsadasyvam mahe kṣatrāya jinvathaḥ ||
english: Come to us, O wealth-possessing lords of prizes, along the paths of Ṛta; with those [paths] by which, O bulls, you quicken Tṛkṣi and Trasadasyu to great dominion.

sanskrit: ayaṁ vām adribhiḥ sutaḥ somo narā vṛṣaṇvasū | ā yātaṁ somapītaye pibataṁ dāśuṣo gṛhe ||
english: This soma, O men, O lords with strong bulls, has been pressed for you with the pressing-stones; come to drink the soma; drink it in the house of the worshipper.

sanskrit: ā hi ruhutam aśvinā rathe kośe hiraṇyaye vṛṣaṇvasū | yuñjāthām pīvarīr iṣaḥ ||
english: Mount, O Aśvins, the golden-bodied chariot, O lords with strong bulls; harness the nourishing draughts [of refreshment].

sanskrit: yābhiḥ paktham avatho yābhir adhriguṁ yābhir babhruṁ vijoṣasam | tābhir no makṣū tūyam aśvinā gatam bhiṣajyataṁ yad āturam ||
english: With those [aids] by which you helped Paktha, with those by which [you helped] Adhrigu, with those by which [you helped] Babhru to be well-pleased — with those, O Aśvins, come quickly and swiftly to us, and heal whatever is afflicted.

sanskrit: yad adhrigāvo adhrigū idā cid ahno aśvinā havāmahe | vayaṁ gīrbhir vipanyavaḥ ||
english: Even now at this very moment of the day, O Aśvins, O lords who hold unswerving cattle, we call upon you — we who celebrate [you] with songs and praises.

sanskrit: tābhir ā yātaṁ vṛṣaṇopa me havaṁ viśvapsuṁ viśvavāryam | iṣā maṁhiṣṭhā purubhūtamā narā yābhiḥ kriviṁ vāvṛdhus tābhir ā gatam ||
english: Come with those [aids] to my all-containing, all-excellent call, O bulls, most bountiful and most praised of all, O men; with those by which you made Kṛvi to prosper — with those come hither.

sanskrit: tāv idā cid ahānāṁ tāv aśvinā vandamāna upa bruve | tā u namobhir īmahe ||
english: Even now in these very days, I call upon those two praised Aśvins close [to me]; those two we implore also with our homage.

sanskrit: tāv id doṣā tā uṣasi śubhas patī tā yāman rudravartanī | mā no martāya ripave vājinīvasū paro rudrāv ati khyatam ||
english: Those two [are present] at dusk, those two at dawn, those two lords of beauty, those two who travel on a dread path; do not look beyond us, O lords of prizes, toward any mortal enemy — [you] two Rudras.

sanskrit: ā sugmyāya sugmyam prātā rathenāśvinā vā sakṣaṇī | huve piteva sobharī ||
english: For the pleasant journey, [come] on a pleasant [chariot] at dawn, O Aśvins, or [come] as companions; I invoke [you], Sobhari, as a son [invokes] a father.

sanskrit: manojavasā vṛṣaṇā madacyutā makṣuṁgamābhir ūtibhiḥ | ārāttāc cid bhūtam asme avase pūrvībhiḥ purubhojasā ||
english: Swift as thought, O bulls, whose ecstasy is overwhelming, with your swiftly-moving aids — even from afar be present for our protection with your many former [gifts], O all-nourishing ones.

sanskrit: ā no aśvāvad aśvinā vartir yāsiṣṭam madhupātamā narā | gomad dasrā hiraṇyavat ||
english: Come to us, O Aśvins, on the best path with horses, O men who drink the sweetest [draught]; [bring] cattle and gold, O wondrous ones.

sanskrit: suprāvargaṁ suvīryaṁ suṣṭhu vāryam anādhṛṣṭaṁ rakṣasvinā | asminn ā vām āyāne vājinīvasū viśvā vāmāni dhīmahi ||
english: In this your approach, O lords of prizes, possessing good ambrosia-glory, good heroic force, excellent desirable [gifts], unconquered and potent, may we establish all good things.

sanskrit: īḷiṣvā hi pratīvyaṁ yajasva jātavedasam | cariṣṇudhūmam agṛbhītaśociṣam ||
english: Praise and worship Jātavedas directly: the one whose smoke moves freely, whose flame is unconstrained.

sanskrit: dāmānaṁ viśvacarṣaṇe 'gniṁ viśvamano girā | uta stuṣe viṣpardhaso rathānām ||
english: With my song I praise Agni, the bond for all peoples and of all-embracing mind, and also [as] the swift one of chariots racing together.

sanskrit: yeṣām ābādha ṛgmiya iṣaḥ pṛkṣaś ca nigrabhe | upavidā vahnir vindate vasu ||
english: The oblation-bearer who is a friend in distress, whose hymn-worthy impulses and nourishments are within his grasp — [such a one] finds wealth.

sanskrit: ud asya śocir asthād dīdiyuṣo vy ajaram | tapurjambhasya sudyuto gaṇaśriyaḥ ||
english: The flame of the blazing, ageless one has risen up, [the flame] of him of glowing jaws, of beautiful radiance, adorned by [his] host [of flames].

sanskrit: ud u tiṣṭha svadhvara stavāno devyā kṛpā | abhikhyā bhāsā bṛhatā śuśukvaṇiḥ ||
english: Rise up, O performer of right sacrifice, praised and glowing with divine beauty; look upon [us] with thy great radiance, O blazing one.

sanskrit: agne yāhi suśastibhir havyā juhvāna āṇuṣak | yathā dūto babhūtha havyavāhanaḥ ||
english: Come, O Agni, with well-composed praises, offering the oblations in continuous succession, as thou hast become the messenger and carrier of the offering.

sanskrit: agniṁ vaḥ pūrvyaṁ huve hotāraṁ carṣaṇīnām | tam ayā vācā gṛṇe tam u vaḥ stuṣe ||
english: I invoke for you the ancient Agni, the hotar of the peoples; I celebrate him with this voice, and for you I praise him.

sanskrit: yajñebhir adbhutakratum yaṁ kṛpā sūdayanta it | mitraṁ na jane sudhitam ṛtāvani ||
english: Him of wondrous purpose who is purified by [their] grace through sacrifices, well-established like Mitra among [his] people, the guardian of ṛta.

sanskrit: ṛtāvānam ṛtāyavo yajñasya sādhanam girā | upo enaṁ jujuṣur namasas pade ||
english: Those who follow ṛta have rejoiced with their song in the upholder of ṛta, the perfector of the sacrifice, at the place of homage.

sanskrit: acchā no aṅgirastamaṁ yajñāso yantu saṁyataḥ | hotā yo asti vikṣv ā yaśastam aḥ ||
english: Let our sacrifices go straight to him who is most Aṅgiras-like, who is the hotar most worthy of praise among the clans.

sanskrit: agne tava tye ajarendhānāso bṛhad bhāḥ | aśvā iva vṛṣaṇas taviṣīyavaḥ ||
english: O Agni, those who kindle thee, thy ageless ones, [display] great brilliance; they are like stallions possessed of force and vigor.

sanskrit: sa tvaṁ na ūrjām pate rayiṁ rāsva suvīryam | prāva nas toke tanaye samatsu ā ||
english: So do thou, O lord of vigours, bestow upon us wealth with excellent heroic force; protect us, our offspring, our progeny, in battles.

sanskrit: yad vā u viśpatiḥ śitaḥ suprīto manuṣo viśi | viśved agniḥ prati rakṣāṁsi sedhati ||
english: When the lord of the clan, alert and well-pleased, is [present] among the people of Manu, Agni wards off all demons.

sanskrit: śruṣṭy agne navasya me stomasya vīra viśpate | ni māyinas tapuṣā rakṣaso daha ||
english: Hear, O Agni, my new hymn of praise, O hero, lord of the clan; burn down the deceitful demons with thy heat.

sanskrit: na tasya māyayā cana ripur īśīta martyaḥ | yo agnaye dadāśa havyadātibhiḥ ||
english: No mortal enemy shall have power over him through trickery — over the one who has served Agni with his gift of oblations.

sanskrit: vyaśvas tvā vasuvidam ukṣaṇyur apṛṇād ṛṣiḥ | maho rāye tam u tvā sam idhīmahi ||
english: The seer Vyaśva, who desired cattle, satisfied thee, O finder of wealth; for great riches we too would kindle thee.

sanskrit: uśanā kāvyas tvā ni hotāram asādayat | āyajiṁ tvā manave jātavedasam ||
english: Uśanā Kāvya established thee as hotar; [he established thee,] Jātavedas, who obtains [the sacrifice] for Manu.

sanskrit: viśve hi tvā sajoṣaso devāso dūtam akrata | śruṣṭī deva prathamo yajñiyo bhuvaḥ ||
english: All the gods in agreement have made thee their messenger; through [their] hearing, O god, thou hast become foremost and worthy of sacrifice.

sanskrit: imaṁ ghā vīro amṛtaṁ dūtaṁ kṛṇvīta martyaḥ | pāvakaṁ kṛṣṇavartaniṁ vihāyasam ||
english: A hero among mortals would indeed make this immortal one his messenger — the purifier who travels on the black track, [soaring] through the air.

sanskrit: taṁ huvema yatasrucaḥ subhāsaṁ śukraśociṣam | viśām agnim ajaraṁ pratnam īḍyam ||
english: Him we invoke with uplifted ladles: the brightly shining one of pure radiance, the ageless, ancient Agni of the clans, worthy of praise.

sanskrit: yo asmai havyadātibhir āhutim marto avidhut | bhūri poṣaṁ sa dhatte vīravad yaśaḥ ||
english: The mortal who has brought an oblation to him [Agni] with gifts of offering — he secures abundant nourishment and glory with heroic power.

sanskrit: prathamaṁ jātavedasam agniṁ yajñeṣu pūrvyam | prati srug eti namasā haviṣmatī ||
english: The offering-ladle, full of the oblation, approaches with homage the foremost Jātavedas, Agni, the most ancient in sacrifices.

sanskrit: ābhir vidhemāgnaye jyeṣṭhābhir vyaśvavat | maṁhiṣṭhābhir matibhiḥ śukraśociṣe ||
english: With these, the greatest [thoughts], most bountiful, like those of Vyaśva, may we serve Agni, the one of pure radiance.

sanskrit: nūnam arca vihāyase stomedhi sthūrayūpavat | ṛṣe vaiyaśva damyāyāgnaye ||
english: Sing now to the sky-traverser with hymns like those of Sthūrayūpa; O seer of the line of Vyaśva, [sing] to Agni the tamer [of foes].

sanskrit: atithim mānuṣāṇāṁ sūnuṁ vanaspatīnām | viprā agnim avase pratnam īḻate ||
english: The inspired poets implore the ancient Agni, the guest of men and son of the forest trees, for protection.

sanskrit: maho viśvām̐ abhi ṣato 'bhi havyāni mānuṣā | agne ni ṣatsi namasādhi barhiṣi ||
english: O Agni, sitting before all the great [gods] and before the human oblations, seat thyself upon the sacred grass with homage.

sanskrit: vaṁsvā no vāryā puru vaṁsva rāyaḥ puruspṛhaḥ | suvīryasya prajāvato yaśasvataḥ ||
english: Win for us many desirable things; win for us wealth much longed-for, with excellent heroic force, with offspring, and with renown.

sanskrit: tvaṁ varo suṣāmṇe 'gne janāya codaya | sadā vaso rātiṁ yaviṣṭha śaśvate ||
english: Thou art the best, O Agni; rouse the people to prosperity; bestow thy gift always and perpetually, O youngest [one], O lord of wealth.

sanskrit: tvaṁ hi supratūr asi tvaṁ no gomatīr iṣaḥ | maho rāyaḥ sātim agne apā vṛdhi ||
english: Thou art indeed easy to call upon; grant us impulses rich in cattle; increase the winning of great wealth, O Agni.

sanskrit: agne tvaṁ yaśā asy ā mitrāvaruṇā vaha | ṛtāvānā samrājā pūtadakṣasā ||
english: O Agni, thou art glorious; bring hither Mitra and Varuṇa, the upholders of ṛta, the two sovereign lords of pure discernment.

sanskrit: sakhāya ā śiṣāmahi brahmendrāya vajriṇe | stuṣa ū ṣu vo nṛtamāya dhṛṣṇave ||
english: Friends, let us recite the sacred word for Indra the vajra-bearer; I praise for you him who is foremost among men, the bold one.

sanskrit: śavasā hy asi śruto vṛtrahattena vṛtrahā | maghair maghono ati śūra dāśasi ||
english: For thou art renowned for might, the slayer of Vṛtra by thy slaying of Vṛtra; O hero, thou surpassest the generous with thy bounties.

sanskrit: sa naḥ stavāna ā bhara rayiṁ citraśravastamam | nireke cid yo harivo vasur dadiḥ ||
english: While being praised, bring to us the wealth most brilliant in fame; for thou, O bay-horsed one, art the wealth-giver even in isolation.

sanskrit: ā nirekam uta priyam indra darṣi janānām | dhṛṣatā dhṛṣṇo stavamāna ā bhara ||
english: Bring hither what is apart [from others] and what is dear [to us] among the [goods] of peoples, O Indra; being praised, bring [it] boldly, O bold one.

sanskrit: na te savyaṁ na dakṣiṇaṁ hastaṁ varanta āmuraḥ | na paribādho harivo gaviṣṭiṣu ||
english: The hasty ones cannot restrain thy left hand nor thy right hand, O bay-horsed lord; no obstruction [holds thee back] in the quest for cattle.

sanskrit: ā tvā gobhir iva vrajaṁ gīrbhir ṛṇomy adrivaḥ | ā smā kāmaṁ jaritur ā manaḥ pṛṇa ||
english: I drive thee with my songs as [one drives] cattle toward the pen, O stone-wielder; fill full the desire and the mind of the praiser.

sanskrit: viśvāni viśvamanaso dhiyā no vṛtrahantama | ugra praṇetar adhi ṣū vaso gahi ||
english: With thy all-embracing mind, with our thought, O foremost slayer of Vṛtra, come here above us, O terrible leader, O lord of wealth.

sanskrit: vayaṁ te asya vṛtrahan vidyāma śūra navyasaḥ | vasoḥ spārhasya puruhūta rādhhasaḥ ||
english: May we know of thee, O slayer of Vṛtra, O hero, the latest [bounty] — of the wealth most to be desired, O much-invoked Indra, of the bounty.

sanskrit: indra yathā hy asti te 'parītaṁ nṛto śavaḥ | amṛktā rātiḥ puruhūta dāśuṣe ||
english: O Indra, as it is — truly thy strength is unlimited, O manly one; thy gift for the worshipper is undiminished, O much-invoked one.

sanskrit: ā vṛṣasva mahāmaha mahe nṛtama rādhase | dṛḻhaś cid dṛhya maghavan magattataye ||
english: Rain down, O great lord, for great bounty, O most manly one; make [us] firm even in the firm [battle], O bountiful one, so that we may obtain thy gifts.

sanskrit: nū anyatrā cid adrivas tvan no jagmur āśasaḥ | maghavañ chagdhi tava tan na ūtibhiḥ ||
english: Now our hopes have gone nowhere but to thee, O stone-wielder; fulfil that for us, O bountiful one, with thy aids.

sanskrit: nahy aṅga nṛto tvad anyaṁ vindāmi rādhase | rāye dyumnāya śavase ca girvaṇaḥ ||
english: Truly, O manly one, I find no other than thee for bounty, for wealth, for brilliance, and for might, O lover of praise.

sanskrit: endum indrāya siñcata pibāti somyaṁ madhu | pra rādhhasā codayāte mahitvanā ||
english: Pour out the soma-drop for Indra; he drinks the sweet soma-honey; drive [us] forward with his bounty and his greatness.

sanskrit: upo harīṇāṁ patim dakṣaṁ pṛñcantam abravam | nūnaṁ śrudhi stuvato aśvyasya ||
english: I addressed the lord of the bay horses who mingles discernment [with action]: hear now the praise of him who sings of horses.

sanskrit: nahy aṅga purā cana jajñe vīrataras tvat | nakī rāyā naivathā na bhandanā ||
english: Truly, never in former times was one born more heroic than thee; none [is equal to thee] in wealth, nor in power, nor in the bestowing of gifts.

sanskrit: ed u madhvo madintaraṁ siñca vādhvaryo andhasaḥ | evā hi vīraḥ stavate sadāvṛdhaḥ ||
english: Pour forth something more intoxicating of the sweet mead, O adhvaryu; for thus is the ever-waxing hero praised.

sanskrit: indra sthātar harīṇāṁ nakiṣ ṭe pūrvyastutim | ud ānaṁśa śavasā na bhandanā ||
english: O Indra, master of the bay horses, no one has reached thy ancient glory in might, nor in the giving of gifts.

sanskrit: taṁ vo vājānāṁ patim ahūmahi śravasyavaḥ | aprāyubhir yajñebhir vāvṛdhenyam ||
english: Him, the lord of prizes, we call upon for you — we who seek fame — the one to be strengthened with unwearied sacrifices.

sanskrit: eto nv indraṁ stavāma sakhāyaḥ stomyaṁ naram | kṛṣṭīr yo viśvā abhy asty ekat ||
english: Come now, O friends, let us praise Indra, the man worthy of hymns, who alone overreaches all the peoples.

sanskrit: agorudhāya gaviṣe dyukṣāya dasmyaṁ vacaḥ | ghṛtāt svādīyo madhunaś ca vocata ||
english: Speak the wondrous word to him who does not hoard cattle, who seeks cattle, who is heavenly — sweeter than ghee and sweeter than honey.

sanskrit: yasyāmitāni vīryā na rādhaḥ paryetave | jyotir na viśvam abhy asti dakṣiṇā ||
english: He whose heroic deeds are immeasurable, whose bounty is not to be encompassed — the gift of his right hand pervades all things like light.

sanskrit: stuhīndraṁ vyaśvavad anūrmiṁ vājinaṁ yamam | aryo gayam maṁhamānaṁ vi dāśuṣe ||
english: Praise Indra like Vyaśva: him of unwavering waves, the prize-winner, the controller, the noble one who bestows wealth upon the worshipper.

sanskrit: evā nūnam upa stuhi vaiyaśva daśamaṁ navam | suvidvāṁsaṁ carkṛtyaṁ caraṇīnām ||
english: Even thus, O descendant of Vyaśva, praise him now for the tenth and ninth time: the one who knows well and is ever-active among those who move about.

sanskrit: vetthā hi nirṛtīnāṁ vajrahasta pari vṛjam | ahar-ahaḥ śundhyuḥ paripādām iva ||
english: For thou knowest the avoidance of calamities, O vajra-handed one, day by day — as the purifier [knows] the circuit of [his] steps.

sanskrit: tad indrāva ā bhara yenā daṁsiṣṭha kṛtvane | dvitā kutsāya śiśnatho ni codaya ||
english: Bring that, O Indra, for our gain, O most wondrous one; impel [us] to action; spur Kutsa twofold for his deeds.

sanskrit: tam u tvā nūnam īmahe navyaṁ daṁsiṣṭha sanyase | sa tvaṁ no viśvā abhimātīḥ sakṣaṇiḥ ||
english: We implore thee now with new [praise], O most wondrous one, for the gaining [of wealth]; so thou shalt overcome all hostile assaults upon us.

sanskrit: ya ṛkṣād aṁhaso mucad yo vāryāt sapta sindhuṣu | vadhar dāsasya tuvinṛmṇa nīnamaḥ ||
english: He who releases from hardship in the bear-[haunted realm], who [delivers] from danger in the seven rivers — O mighty-spirited one, we have bent down the weapon of the Dāsa.

sanskrit: yathā varo suṣāmṇe sanibhyam āvaho rayim | vyaśvebhyaḥ subhage vājinīvati ||
english: As thou didst bring wealth to the excellent-song [singer] for the gaining [thereof], to the [descendants] of Vyaśva, O blessed one, O possessor of prize-winning steeds.

sanskrit: ā nāryasya dakṣiṇā vyaśvām̐ etu somin aḥ | sthūraṁ ca rādhaḥ śatavat sahasravat ||
english: May the gift of the right hand of the noble one go to the soma-pressing descendants of Vyaśva — the abundant bounty, a hundredfold, a thousandfold.

sanskrit: yat tvā pṛcchād ījānaḥ kuhayā kuhayākṛte | eṣo apaśrito valo gomatīm ava tiṣṭhati ||
english: When the sacrificer asks thee, led astray by a deceiver and a deceiving deed, [say:] this Vala, when laid open, stands [revealed] before the cow-rich [realm].

sanskrit: tā vāṁ viśvasya gopā devā deveṣu yajñiyā | ṛtāvānā yajase pūtadakṣasā ||
english: Those two of you, O gods worthy of sacrifice among the gods, O guardians of all, O upholders of ṛta and of pure discernment, I sacrifice to you.

sanskrit: mitrā tanā na rathyā varuṇo yaś ca sukratuḥ | sanāt sujātā tanayā dhṛtavratā ||
english: Mitra and Varuṇa — their bond is like that of chariot-fellows — and he of good purpose; from of old well-born, [their] offspring, keepers of their vow.

sanskrit: tā mātā viśvavedasāsuryāya pramahasa | mahī jajānāditir ṛtāvarī ||
english: The great Aditi, the mother of all knowledge and of divine power, the one abounding in ṛta, bore those two of boundless greatness.

sanskrit: mahāntā mitrāvaruṇā samrājā devāv asurā | ṛtāvānāv ṛtam ā ghoṣato bṛhat ||
english: The great Mitra and Varuṇa, the two sovereign lords, divine Asuras, upholders of ṛta, proclaim ṛta with a great voice.

sanskrit: napātā śavaso mahaḥ sūnū dakṣasya sukratū | sṛpradānū iṣo vāstv adhi kṣitaḥ ||
english: Grandsons of great might, sons of Dakṣa, of good purpose, givers of flowing [gifts], sitters upon the dwelling-place of nourishments.

sanskrit: saṁ yā dānūni yemathuḥ divyāḥ pārthivīr iṣaḥ | nabhasvatīr ā vāṁ carantu vṛṣṭayaḥ ||
english: You two have brought together the divine and earthly nourishments; may the cloud-bearing rains come to you.

sanskrit: adhi yā bṛhato divo 'bhi yūtheva paśyataḥ | ṛtāvānā samrājā namase hitā ||
english: They who look down from the great heaven as [a herdsman looks] over his herd — the two upholders of ṛta, the sovereign lords, devoted to homage.

sanskrit: ṛtāvānā ni ṣedatuḥ sāmrājyāya sukratū | dhṛtavratā kṣatriyā kṣatram āśatuḥ ||
english: The two upholders of ṛta, of good purpose, have sat down for sovereign rule; the keepers of their vow, the rulers, have attained dominion.

sanskrit: akṣṇaś cid gātuvittarān ulbaṇena cakṣasā | ni cin miṣantā nicirā ni cikyatuḥ ||
english: With glaring eye [they watch], more knowledgeable than even the eye itself [in finding] a path; unblinking and sharp-sighted, they have discerned everything.

sanskrit: uta no devy aditir uruṣyatāṁ nāsatyā | uruṣyantu maruto vṛddhaśavasaḥ ||
english: And may the divine Aditi protect us and [may] the Nāsatyās [protect us]; may the Maruts of grown might protect us.

sanskrit: te no nāvam uruṣyata divā naktaṁ sudānavaḥ | ariṣyanto ni pāyubhiḥ sacemahi ||
english: May those good givers protect our ship by day and by night; may we, unharmed, remain under [their] guard.

sanskrit: aghna te viṣṇave vayam ariṣyantaḥ sudānave | śrudhi svayāvan sindho pūrvacittaye ||
english: Unharmed, to thee, O Viṣṇu, O good giver, we address [our prayer]; hear, O self-moving river Sindhu, for [thy] ancient understanding.

sanskrit: tad vāryaṁ vṛṇīmahe variṣṭhaṁ gopayatyam | mitro yat pānti varuṇo yad aryamā ||
english: We choose that most excellent, desirable [protection] which guards — what Mitra guards, what Varuṇa guards, what Aryamā guards.

sanskrit: uta naḥ sindhur apāṁ tan marutas tad aśvinā | indro viṣṇur mīḍhvāṁsaḥ sajoṣasaḥ ||
english: And may the Sindhu of the waters grant us that; the Maruts, the Aśvins, Indra, Viṣṇu — all the generous ones in unison.

sanskrit: te hi ṣmā vanuṣo naro 'bhimātiṁ kayasya cit | tigmaṁ na kṣodaḥ pratighnanti bhūrṇayaḥ ||
english: For those men who are eager [to please them] strike back the hostile designs of any whatsoever — [fierce] as the raging current strikes back — they are impetuous.

sanskrit: ayam eka itthā purūru caṣṭe vi viśpatiḥ | tasya vratāny anu vaś carāmasi ||
english: This one sovereign lord truly sees widely and abundantly; following his ordinances do we move.

sanskrit: anu pūrvāṇy okyā sāmrājyasya saścima | mitrasya vratā varuṇasya dīrghaśrut ||
english: We follow the ancient, well-known [ordinances] of the sovereign rule — the vows of Mitra and Varuṇa, heard far and wide.

sanskrit: pari yo raśminā divo 'ntān mame pṛthivyāḥ | ubhe ā paprau rodasī mahitvā ||
english: He who has measured with his cord the boundaries of heaven and earth, who has filled both the world-halves with his greatness.

sanskrit: ud u ṣya śaraṇe divo jyotir ayaṁsta sūryaḥ | agnir na śukraḥ samidhāna āhutaḥ ||
english: The sun has raised up the light in the shelter of heaven; like Agni bright, once kindled and invoked.

sanskrit: vaco dīrghaprasadmanīśe vājasya gomataḥ | īśe hi pitvo 'viṣasya dāvane ||
english: He is lord of speech whose dwelling-place is vast, lord of the prize rich in cattle; he is the lord of the invigorating nourishment to give.

sanskrit: tat sūryaṁ rodasī ubhe doṣā vastor upa bruve | bhojeṣv asmām̐ abhy uc carā sadā ||
english: That sun I invoke before both world-halves, at evening and at morning; always shine upon us among the generous ones.

sanskrit: ṛjram ukṣaṇyāyane rajataṁ harayāṇe | rathaṁ yuktam asanāma suṣāmaṇi ||
english: The gleaming [bull] on its path, the silver-bright on the golden [track] — may we obtain the yoked chariot in the good soma [pressing].

sanskrit: tā me aśvyānāṁ harīṇāṁ nitocanā | uto nu kṛtvyānāṁ nṛvāhasā ||
english: Those two who urge on [the steeds] of horses, [those who guide] the bay horses — and also the man-carrying [bay steeds] of [those] who act [heroically].

sanskrit: smad abhīśū kaśāvantā viprā naviṣṭhayā matī | maho vājināv arvantā sacāsanam ||
english: With gleaming reins and whips, with the freshest inspired thought, the two great prize-winning coursers are seated together.

sanskrit: yuvor u ṣū rathaṁ huve sadhastutyāya sūriṣu | atūrtadakṣā vṛṣaṇā vṛṣaṇvasū ||
english: I call your chariot for the common praise among the patrons; [you] of unweakened power, O bulls, O lords with strong bulls.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ varo suṣāmṇe mahe tane nāsatyā | avobhir yātho vṛṣaṇā vṛṣaṇvasū ||
english: You two are the best for [him of] excellent soma-song, for great offspring, O Nāsatyās; come with your aids, O bulls, O lords with strong bulls.

sanskrit: tā vām adya havāmahe havyebhir vājinīvasū | pūrvīr iṣa iṣayantāv ati kṣapaḥ ||
english: We call upon you two today with our oblations, O lords of prizes; [you who] quicken the many impulses through the nights.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ vāhiṣṭho aśvinā ratho yātu śruto narā | upa stomān turasya darśathaḥ śriye ||
english: May your swiftest chariot come, O renowned Aśvins, O men; you appear at the praises of Tura for [his] glory.

sanskrit: juhurāṇā cid aśvinā manyethāṁ vṛṣaṇvasū | yuvaṁ hi rudrā parṣatho ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: Even while going astray, O Aśvins, you two would be well-disposed, O lords with strong bulls; for you two, O Rudras, carry [us] beyond our foes.

sanskrit: dasrā hi viśvam ānuṣaṅ makṣūbhiḥ paridīyathaḥ | dhiyaṁjinvā madhuvarṇā śubhas patī ||
english: For you wonders travel continually around everything with swiftness; quickeners of thought, honey-bright, lords of beauty.

sanskrit: upa no yātam aśvinā rāyā viśvapuṣā saha | maghavānā suvīrāv anapacyutā ||
english: Come to us, O Aśvins, together with wealth that nourishes all, O bountiful ones with excellent heroic force, ever-steadfast.

sanskrit: ā me asya pratīvyam indranāsatyā gatam | devā devebhir adya sacanastamā ||
english: Come toward me directly for this, O Indra and Nāsatyās; today, O gods, [come] to the gods as the most helpful companions.

sanskrit: vayaṁ hi vāṁ havāmaha ukṣaṇyanto vyaśvavat | sumatibhir upa viprāv ihā gatam ||
english: For we call upon you two, seeking cattle-wealth like the [descendants] of Vyaśva; come hither, O inspired ones, with your benevolences.

sanskrit: aśvinā sv ṛṣe stuhi kuvit te śravato havam | nedīyasaḥ kūḻayātaḥ paṇīṁr uta ||
english: O seer, praise the Aśvins well; perchance [they] who drive by swiftly will hear the call — even from nearer than the Paṇis.

sanskrit: vaiyaśvasya śrutaṁ naro uto me asya vedathaḥ | sajoṣasā varuṇo mitro aryamā ||
english: You men know the fame of the descendant of Vyaśva and know of this [hymn] of mine; Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryamā [are] in accord.

sanskrit: yuvādattasya dhiṣṇyā yuvānitasya sūribhiḥ | ahar-ahar vṛṣaṇa mahyaṁ śikṣatam ||
english: O bulls, instruct me day by day in what has been given by you and what has been brought by you among the patrons.

sanskrit: yo vāṁ yajñebhir āvṛto 'dhivastrā vadhūr iva | saparyantā śubhe cakrāte aśvinā ||
english: He who is enveloped by your sacrifices like a bride clothed in garments — he who serves you two has caused beauty [to be made], O Aśvins.

sanskrit: yo vām uruvyacastamaṁ ciketati nṛpāyyam | vartir aśvinā pari yātam asmayū ||
english: He who perceives your most wide-ranging [bounty] worthy of men, to him, O Aśvins, come round on your course, eager for us.

sanskrit: asmabhyaṁ su vṛṣaṇvasū yātaṁ vartir nṛpāyyam | viṣudruhe va yajñam ūhathur girā ||
english: Come to us well, O lords with strong bulls, on your course worthy of men; as if against traitors you have borne our sacrifice with your song.

sanskrit: vāhiṣṭho vāṁ havānāṁ stomo dūto huvan narā | yuvābhyām bhūtv aśvinā ||
english: The hymn of praise, the best bearer of your invocations, shall be the messenger calling [you], O men; let it belong to you two, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: yad ado divo arṇava iṣo vā madatho gṛhe | śrutam in me amartyā ||
english: Whether you two are in that ocean of heaven, or taking joy in [your] home with refreshments — hear, O immortal ones, this [hymn] of mine.

sanskrit: uta syā śvetayāvarī vāhiṣṭhā vāṁ nadīnām | sindhu hiraṇyavartaniḥ ||
english: And this white-coursing [river], the best bearer among the rivers — the Sindhu with her golden track.

sanskrit: smad etayā sukīrtyāśvinā śvetayā dhiyā | vahithe śubhrayāvānā ||
english: With this good fame, O Aśvins, with this white thought, you two who travel brightly shall carry [us].

sanskrit: yukṣvā hi tvaṁ rathāsahā yuvasva poṣyā vaso | ān no vāyo madhu pibāsmākaṁ savanā gahi ||
english: Harness, O Vāyu, the chariot-supporters, yoke the nourishing ones, O lord of wealth; come and drink the sweet [soma] of ours; come to our soma-pressings.

sanskrit: tava vāyav ṛtaspate tvaṣṭur jāmātar adbhuta | avāṁsy ā vṛṇīmahe ||
english: Thy aids, O Vāyu, lord of ṛta, O wondrous son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, we choose [for ourselves].

sanskrit: tvaṣṭur jāmātaraṁ vayam īśānaṁ rāya īmahe | sutāvanto vāyuṁ dyumnā janāsaḥ ||
english: We, the people who have pressed the soma, brilliant [in song], implore the son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, the lord of wealth — Vāyu.

sanskrit: vāyo yāhi śivā divo vahasvā su svaśvyam | vahasva mahaḥ pṛthupakṣasā rathe ||
english: Come, O Vāyu, with auspicious [gifts] from heaven; carry well [the omen of] good horses; carry [us] with great, broad-winged [speed] in thy chariot.

sanskrit: tvāṁ hi supsar astamaṁ nṛṣadaneṣu hūmahe | grāvāṇaṁ nāśvapṛṣṭham maṁhanā ||
english: Thee, the most easy to find a place with among the places of men, we invoke — like the pressing-stone, not [like one who rides] on the horse's back, with generosity.

sanskrit: sa tvaṁ no deva manasā vāyo mandāno agriyaḥ | kṛdhi vājām̐ apo dhiyaḥ ||
english: So do thou, O god Vāyu, in thy mind, rejoicing as the foremost one, grant us prizes; drive forward [our] thoughts.

sanskrit: agnir ukthe purohito grāvāṇo barhir adhvare | ṛcā yāmi maruto brahmaṇas patim devām̐ avo vareṇyam ||
english: Agni is appointed hotar in the recitation, the pressing-stones and sacred grass at the sacrifice; with my verse I approach the Maruts, the lord of the sacred word, the gods, the most excellent help.

sanskrit: ā paśuṁ gāsi pṛthivīṁ vanapatīn uṣāsā naktam oṣadhīḥ | viśve ca no vasavo viśvavedaso dhīnām bhūta prāvitāraḥ ||
english: Thou encompassest cattle, earth, forest trees, Dawn and Night, the plants; and may all of you, O Vasus, all-knowing, be the promoters of our thoughts.

sanskrit: pra sū na etv adhvaro 'gnā deveṣu pūrvyaḥ | ādityeṣu pra varuṇe dhṛtavrate marutsu viśvabhānuṣu ||
english: Let our sacrifice go forward among the gods, the ancient one [proceeding] to Agni; [let it go] to Varuṇa the keeper of his vow among the Ādityas, and to the Maruts of all-pervading radiance.

sanskrit: viśve hi ṣmā manave viśvavedaso bhuvan vṛdhe riśādasaḥ | ariṣṭebhiḥ pāyubhir viśvavedaso yantā no 'vṛkaṁ chardiḥ ||
english: For all of them, all-knowing and devouring enemies, truly existed for the growth of Manu; with uninjured guardianship, all-knowing, may they lead us to a safe shelter.

sanskrit: ā no adya samanaso gantā viśve sajoṣasaḥ | ṛcā girā maruto devy adite sadane pastye mahi ||
english: Come to us today, all of you with one mind, all in accord; with verse and song, O Maruts, O divine Aditi, [come] to our great domestic dwelling.

sanskrit: abhi priyā maruto yā vo aśvyā havyā mitra prayāthana | ā barhir indro varuṇas turā narā ādityāsaḥ sadantu naḥ ||
english: Come, O Maruts, toward the dear [offerings] and those of yours that are equine — the oblations, O Mitra; let Indra, Varuṇa, the swift men, the Ādityas, sit down on our sacred grass.

sanskrit: vayaṁ vo vṛktabarhiṣo hitaprayasa ānuṣak | sutasomāso varuṇa havāmahe manuṣvad iddhāgnayaḥ ||
english: We, with strewn sacred grass, with offerings set in place, in succession, with pressed soma, O Varuṇa, we call upon you — with fires kindled as in the [time of] Manu.

sanskrit: ā pra yāta maruto viṣṇo aśvinā pūṣan mākīnayā dhiyā | indra ā yātu prathamaḥ saniṣyubhir vṛṣā yo vṛtrahā gṛṇe ||
english: Come forward, O Maruts, Viṣṇu, Aśvins, Pūṣan, with no niggardly thought; let Indra come first with his prize-winning [powers] — the bull whom I praise as the slayer of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: vi no devāso adruho 'cchidraṁ śarma yacchata | na yad dūrād vasavo nū cid antito varūtham āda dharṣati ||
english: Protect us, O gods, free of malice, with unbroken shelter; for no sheltering [power], whether from far or near, even now subdues [the foe], O Vasus.

sanskrit: asti hi vaḥ sajātyaṁ riśādaso devāso asty āpyam | pra ṇaḥ pūrvasmai suvitāya vocata makṣū sumnāya navyase ||
english: There is a community of kind with you, O gods who devour enemies; there is kinship; speak to us for our former well-being, quickly for a newer blessedness.

sanskrit: idā hi va upastutim idā vāmasya bhaktaye | upa vo viśvavedaso namasyur ām̐ asṛkṣy anyām iva ||
english: Now indeed I have sent forth homage to you and now [homage] for the obtaining of the good [gift] — I, who reverently approach you all-knowing ones, as if toward another.

sanskrit: ud u ṣya vaḥ savitā supraṇītayo 'sthād ūrdhvo vareṇyaḥ | ni dvipādaś catuṣpādo arthi no 'viśran patayiṣṇavaḥ ||
english: He, your Savitṛ, O best-guiding ones, has stood up high, most excellent; the two-footed [creatures] and the four-footed ones have come to rest, [and so have] the flying ones who seek their purpose.

sanskrit: devaṁ-devaṁ vo 'vase devaṁ-devam abhiṣṭaye | devaṁ-devaṁ huvema vājasātaye gṛṇanto devyā dhiyā ||
english: Each god among you for protection, each god for favor — each god we call for the winning of prizes, celebrating [each one] with our divine thought.

sanskrit: devāso hi ṣmā manave samanyo viśve sākaṁ sarātayaḥ | te no adya te aparaṁ tuce tuno bhavant u varivo vidaḥ ||
english: For all the gods, with one mind, all together, were truly generous to Manu; may they today and tomorrow, in our want, in our need, be the finders of wide space for us.

sanskrit: pra vaḥ śaṁsāmy adruhaḥ saṁstha upastutīnām | na taṁ dhūrtir varuṇa mitra martyaṁ yo vo dhāmabhyo 'vidhat ||
english: I declare for you, O guileless ones, at the gathering of praises: no deception [afflicts] that mortal, O Varuṇa and Mitra, who has given devotion to your ordinances.

sanskrit: pra sa kṣayaṁ tirate vi mahīr iṣo yo vo varāya dāśati | pra prajābhir jāyate dharmaṇas pary ariṣṭaḥ sarva edhate ||
english: He who gives devotion to your favor extends his dwelling, [gaining] manifold impulses; he is born [abundantly] with offspring according to the law; uninjured, he prospers fully.

sanskrit: ṛte sa vindate yudhaḥ sugebhir yāty adhvanaḥ | aryamā mitro varuṇaḥ sarātayo yaṁ trāyante sajoṣasaḥ ||
english: He finds [success] in battle without [harm], travels the roads by easy [paths] — him whom Aryamā, Mitra, and Varuṇa, generous and in accord, protect.

sanskrit: ajre cid asmai kṛṇuthā nyañcanaṁ durge cid ā susaraṇam | eṣā cid asmād aśaniḥ paro nu sāsredhantī vi naśyatu ||
english: Even in the open field make for him an easy descent [from danger]; even in a narrow pass a good escape; even this thunderbolt that has missed its mark from this [foe] — let it vanish away.

sanskrit: yad adya sūrya udyati priyakṣatrā ṛtaṁ dadha | yan nimruci prabudhi viśvavedaso yad vā madhyaṁdine divaḥ ||
english: What you, O dear-sovereignty ones, establish as ṛta when the sun rises, O all-knowing ones, and at sunset, at awakening, or at midday of the sky —

sanskrit: yad vābhipitve asurā ṛtaṁ yate chardir yema vi dāśuṣe | vayaṁ tad vo vasavo viśvavedasa upa stheyāma madhya ā ||
english: And whatever ṛta you Asuras direct toward [us] at the drawing near of gifts, what shelter you two determine for the worshipper — may we stand in the midst of that, O Vasus, all-knowing.

sanskrit: yad adya sūra udite yan madhyaṁdina ātuci | vāmaṁ dhatha manave viśvavedaso juhvānāya pracetase ||
english: What good [thing] you, all-knowing, place for Manu at the rising of the sun, and at the coming of midday — [you bestow it] upon him who pours the oblation, the wise-minded.

sanskrit: vayaṁ tad vaḥ samrāja ā vṛṇīmahe putro na bahupāyyam | aśyāma tad ādityā juhvato havir yena vasyo 'naśāmahai ||
english: That [bounty] of you sovereign rulers we choose like a son [chooses] what is much to be drunk; may we, O Ādityas, when we pour the oblation, attain that by which we may enjoy better things.

sanskrit: ye triṁśati trayas paro devāso barhir āsadan | vidann aha dvitāsanan ||
english: The gods who, more than thirty-three, have sat on the sacred grass — they found [it], and also sat down in both [realms].

sanskrit: varuṇo mitro aryamā smadrātiṣāco agnayaḥ | patnīvanto vaṣaṭkṛtāḥ ||
english: Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryamā — the fires of memorable generosity — accompanied by their spouses, summoned with the vaṣaṭ-call.

sanskrit: te no gopā apācyas ta udak ta itthā nyak | purastāt sarvayā viśā ||
english: They are our guardians in the south, they in the north, they rightly here below and above — in front with all the folk.

sanskrit: yathā vaśanti devās tathed asat tad eṣāṁ nakir ā minat | arāvā ca na martyaḥ ||
english: As the gods wish, so indeed it shall be; no one diminishes that [will] of theirs; no mortal [is] without their bounty.

sanskrit: saptānāṁ sapta ṛṣṭayaḥ sapta dyumnāny eṣām | sapto adhi śriyo dhire ||
english: Of the seven [groups], seven are their spear-points, seven are their glories; seven are borne upon their splendors.

sanskrit: babhruḥ eko viṣuṇaḥ sūnaro yuvāñjy aṅkte hiraṇyayam ||
english: One [god] is tawny-brown and facing both ways, youthful; he anoints himself with gold.

sanskrit: yonim eka ā sasāda dyotano 'ntar deveṣu medhiraḥ ||
english: One, the shining one, has sat down in the womb [of the altar], the wise one among the gods.

sanskrit: vāśīm eko bibharti hasta āyasīm antar deveṣu nidhrutiḥ ||
english: One holds the iron axe in his hand, the firm one among the gods.

sanskrit: vajram eko bibharti hasta āhitaṁ tena vṛtrāṇi jighnate ||
english: One holds the vajra in his hand, laid ready; with it he strikes down the Vṛtras.

sanskrit: tigmam eko bibharti hasta āyudhaṁ śucir ugro jalāṣabheṣajaḥ ||
english: One holds the sharp weapon in his hand — the pure, terrible one, the healer with cool medicines.

sanskrit: patha ekaḥ pīpāya taskaro yathāṁ eṣa veda nidhīnām ||
english: One watches over the paths as a thief [watches]; he knows the treasures hidden [along the way].

sanskrit: trīṇy eka urugāyo vi cakrame yatra devāso madanti ||
english: One of wide stride has stepped out the three [steps] to where the gods rejoice.

sanskrit: vibhir dvā carataḥ ekayā saha pra pravāseva vasataḥ ||
english: Two travel with the birds, together with one; they dwell as if [going] abroad on a journey.

sanskrit: sado dvā cakrāte upamā divi samrājā sarpirāsutī ||
english: Two have made their seat the highest in heaven, the two sovereign rulers, at the pressing of ghee and soma.

sanskrit: arcanta eke mahi sāma manvata tena sūryam arocayan ||
english: Some, singing, comprehended the great Sāman; by it they made the sun to shine.

sanskrit: nahi vo asty arbhako devāso na kumārakaḥ | viśve satoma hāntait ||
english: There is no one among you who is a small child, O gods, no one who is a mere boy; all of you are truly great.

sanskrit: iti stutāso asathā riśādaso ye stha trayas ca triṁśac ca | manor devā yajñiyāsaḥ ||
english: Having been thus praised, you have been [revealed as] the devourers of enemies — you who are thirty-three, O gods of Manu, worthy of sacrifice.

sanskrit: te nas trādvaṁ te 'vata ta u no adhi vocata | mā naḥ pathaḥ pitryān mānavād adhi dūraṁ naiṣṭa parāvataḥ ||
english: Protect us, help us, and speak above us; do not lead us far away from the ancestral paths of Manu, to a remote distance.

sanskrit: ye devāsa iha sthana viśve vaiśvānarā uta | asmabhyaṁ śarma sapratho gave 'śvāya yacchata ||
english: You gods who stand here, all of you, Vaiśvānara as well — grant to us shelter of broad extent, [shelter for] cattle and horses.
